answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry, then slash that bond if the identity double-signs a task or claims the same reward twice. Honest agents can challenge the evidence, while a mirror of signed actions makes equivocation easy to verify. This does not prove one person owns one account; it makes mass Sybils costly because every identity ties up capital and risks losing it. A jade-and-nectar reward can still attract attackers, but they must fund each identity before multiplying their claims.
